The season marked the addition of two new teams from [[Queensland]]. [[Gold Coast United FC]] and the [[Northern Fury FC|North Queensland Fury FC]] made their A-League debuts at the start of the season.{{cite magazine|url=http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/83528,gold-coast-and-townsville-set-for-aleague.aspx|title=Gold Coast And Townsville Set For A-League|date=28 August 2008|magazine=[[FourFourTwo]]|access-date=5 April 2009|archive-date=29 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029190543/http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/83528,gold-coast-and-townsville-set-for-aleague.aspx|url-status=dead}} Because of this, [[Brisbane Roar FC|Queensland Roar]] were renamed to [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]], as they were no longer the only A-League club from Queensland. With the inception of the two new clubs, many club transfers took place both within Australia and New Zealand, and around the world. The length of the regular season was longer than in previous years, with 27 rounds rather than 21, plus finals. The season began on 6 August, with Melbourne hosting the Central Coast at home.{{cite web |url= http://www.a-league.com.au/site/_content/document/00001133-source.pdf |title= Hyundai A-League 2009/10 Season Draw |access-date= 20 April 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110219222602/http://www.a-league.com.au/site/_content/document/00001133-source.pdf |archive-date= 19 February 2011 |url-status= dead }} {{small|(2.33 [[Megabyte|MB]])}} ''[[Football Federation Australia]]'', 20 April 2009. Retrieved 20 April 2009. As well as these major changes to the league, the [[A-League#Pre-Season Cup|Pre-Season Challenge Cup]] was no longer held as part of the 2009–10 season due to a busier regular season schedule,{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/football/a-league/clubs-ditch-preseason-cup/2009/04/19/1240079538095.html|title=Clubs ditch Pre-Season Cup|last=Hassett|first=Sebastian|date=20 April 2009|newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|access-date=23 April 2009}} and clubs attracting higher profile pre-season friendlies.
